title.zh: 卷431 列傳二百十八 郭松林 李长乐 杨鼎勋 唐殿魁 唐定奎 滕嗣武 骆国忠
title.en: Volume 431 Biographies 218: Guo Songlin, Li Changle, Yang Dingxun, Tang Diankui, Tang Dingkui, Teng Siwu, Luo Guozhong
title.raw: 卷431 列傳二百十八 郭松林 李长乐 杨鼎勋 唐殿魁 唐定奎 滕嗣武 骆国忠

sentences.zh: 列傳二百十八

translations.literal: Biographies 218
translations.idiomatic: Biography 218

sentences.zh: 郭松林李長樂楊鼎勳唐殿魁唐定奎

translations.literal: Guo Songlin, Li Changle, Yang Dingxun, Tang Diankui, Tang Dingkui
translations.idiomatic: Guo Songlin, Li Changle, Yang Dingxun, Tang Diankui, and Tang Dingkui

sentences.zh: 滕嗣武駱國忠

translations.literal: Teng Siwu, Luo Guozhong
translations.idiomatic: Teng Siwu and Luo Guozhong

sentences.zh: 郭松林，字子美，湖南湘潭人。

translations.literal: Guo Songlin, courtesy name Zimei, was a native of Xiangtan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Songlin, style name Zimei, was from Xiangtan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，隸曾國荃軍，從援江西，克安福，從剿永新、太和、萬安、蓮花廳、龍泉，敘獎把總。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he entered Zeng Guoquan's army, followed in the relief of Jiangxi, captured Anfu, joined in suppressing Yongxin, Taihe, Wan'an, Lianhua ting, and Longquan, and was commended with the rank of corporal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he joined Zeng Guoquan's forces, marched to relieve Jiangxi, took Anfu, and helped clear Yongxin, Taihe, Wan'an, Lianhua subprefecture, and Longquan, for which he was commended and given the rank of corporal.

sentences.zh: 進圍吉安府城，七年，石達開率悍黨來援，邀擊於吉水三曲灘，松林首陷陣，多斬獲，收復新喻、峽江、吉水。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Jian prefectural city. In the seventh year Shi Dakai led fierce rebels to relieve it; they were intercepted at Sanqu tan in Jishui. Songlin was first to break the enemy line, killed and captured many, and recovered Xinyu, Xiajiang, and Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the siege of Ji'an. In 1857 Shi Dakai led a fierce rebel force to the relief; Songlin met them at Sanqu tan in Jishui, was first into the enemy ranks, won heavy kills and captures, and recovered Xinyu, Xiajiang, and Jishui.

sentences.zh: 八年，隨克吉安，擢守備。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he took part in capturing Ji'an and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he helped take Ji'an and was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 九年，克景德、浮梁，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he captured Jingde and Fuliang and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he took Jingde and Fuliang and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十年，圍安慶，會剿陳玉成於小池驛，進壁集賢關，每戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he besieged Anqing, joined in suppressing Chen Yucheng at Xiaochi yi, advanced and encamped at Jixian Pass, and won every battle.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he joined the siege of Anqing, fought Chen Yucheng at Xiaochi post station, pushed forward to camp at Jixian Pass, and won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克安慶，擢游擊，賜號奮勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Anqing was taken; he was promoted to battalion commander and granted the title Brave Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Anqing fell; he was promoted to battalion commander and given the title Brave Baturu.

sentences.zh: 克廬江、無為、運漕鎮，下沿江要隘，擢參將。

translations.literal: He captured Lujiang, Wuwei, and Yuncao zhen, took the key passes along the river, and was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took Lujiang, Wuwei, and Yuncao town, seized the vital Yangtze strongpoints, and was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章率淮軍八千赴上海，松林從，與偽忠王李秀成偽慕王譚紹光大戰滬西，破賊眾十萬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang led eight thousand Huai Army troops to Shanghai; Songlin followed. He fought a great battle west of Shanghai against the rebel Loyal King Li Xiucheng and the rebel Princely King Tan Shaoguang and broke a rebel force of one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 Li Hongzhang led eight thousand Huai Army men to Shanghai, and Songlin went with him. West of the city he fought the rebel kings Li Xiucheng and Tan Shaoguang and routed a rebel host of one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 會攻太倉，砲擊城隳，士卒爭進，浮橋斷，賊乘之，死數百人，松林力禦，始得收軍。

translations.literal: In a joint attack on Taicang, cannon fire breached the wall and the troops rushed forward. The pontoon bridge broke; the rebels seized the chance and several hundred men died. Songlin fought hard to hold them off before the army could withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Taicang, artillery smashed the wall and the men surged in. The pontoon bridge gave way; the rebels pressed the opening and several hundred were killed before Songlin fought them off and pulled the force back.

sentences.zh: 二年，克太倉，松林敗賊茜涇、支塘，會克崑山、新陽，以總兵用。

translations.literal: In the second year Taicang was taken. Songlin defeated rebels at Qianjing and Zhitang, joined in taking Kunshan and Xinyang, and was appointed acting major general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 Taicang fell. Songlin beat the rebels at Qianjing and Zhitang, helped take Kunshan and Xinyang, and was appointed acting major general.

sentences.zh: 李秀成合水陸數十萬援江陰，犯常熟，劉銘傳謀乘賊未定擊之。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng united several hundred thousand men by land and water to relieve Jiangyin and threatened Changshu. Liu Mingchuan planned to strike before the rebels had settled in.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng gathered several hundred thousand land and river forces to relieve Jiangyin and menaced Changshu. Liu Mingchuan proposed hitting them before they were fully in position.

sentences.zh: 賊北自北漍，南至張涇橋，東自陳市，西至長壽，縱橫六七十里，築壘憑河，勢大熾。

translations.literal: The rebels ranged from Beigang in the north to Zhangjing Bridge in the south, from Chen shi in the east to Changshou in the west—sixty or seventy li on every side—building forts along the rivers; their power grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stretched from Beigang north to Zhangjing Bridge south and from Chen market east to Changshou west—sixty or seventy li in every direction—throwing up river-line forts until their position was formidable.

sentences.zh: 銘傳進北漍攻其左，松林進南漍攻其右，周盛波等進麥市橋為中路，黃翼升以水師助之。

translations.literal: Mingchuan advanced on Beigang to attack their left; Songlin advanced on Nangang to attack their right; Zhou Shengbo and others advanced on Maishi Bridge as the center; Huang Yisheng aided with the naval force.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan pushed on Beigang against their left flank, Songlin on Nangang against their right, Zhou Shengbo and others up the center at Maishi Bridge, and Huang Yisheng's fleet supported from the water.

sentences.zh: 松林敗賊陳市，越南漍趨張涇，揮刀盪決，血染衣盡赤，賊大潰走。

translations.literal: Songlin defeated the rebels at Chen shi, crossed Nangang toward Zhangjing, swung his blade to cut a path, and blood dyed his clothes completely red; the rebels broke and fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Songlin routed the rebels at Chen market, crossed Nangang toward Zhangjing, and hacked his way through until his clothes were soaked red with blood; the enemy broke and fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 銘傳、盛波等同破賊，自顧山以西皆盡，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: Mingchuan, Shengbo, and the others jointly broke the rebels; west of Gushan all were cleared. Songlin was recorded for appointment as major general.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan, Shengbo, and the rest smashed the rebel line; west of Gushan the enemy was cleared away. Songlin was entered on the rolls for major general.

sentences.zh: 尋克江陰，以提督記名。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jiangyin was taken and he was recorded for appointment as provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin fell soon after, and he was entered on the rolls for provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 又破賊緱山、梅村、麻塘橋，松林受矛傷，既而蘇州、無錫皆复，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: He again defeated rebels at Goushan, Meicun, and Matang Bridge. Songlin was wounded by a spear; thereafter Suzhou and Wuxi were both recovered, and he was given the first-rank official's cap button.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the rebels again at Goushan, Meicun, and Matang Bridge. Songlin took a spear wound; soon Suzhou and Wuxi were recovered, and he received the first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 三年，克宜興、荊溪，敗賊張渚，毀賊壘，收溧陽，解常熟圍，授福山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the third year he captured Yixing and Jingxi, defeated rebels at Zhangzhu, destroyed rebel forts, recovered Liyang, lifted the siege of Changshu, and was appointed major general of Fushan zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he took Yixing and Jingxi, routed the rebels at Zhangzhu, destroyed their forts, recovered Liyang, raised the siege of Changshu, and was made major general of Fushan garrison.

sentences.zh: 大破三河口賊營，賊爭道，六浮橋盡斷，屍塞河，水為不流。

translations.literal: He smashed the rebel camps at Sanhekou. The rebels fought for the road; all six pontoon bridges broke; corpses blocked the river so the water would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: He shattered the rebel camps at Sanhekou. In the scramble for escape all six pontoon bridges collapsed; corpses choked the river until the water barely moved.

sentences.zh: 克常州，進剿浙西，克長興，复湖州，功皆最。

translations.literal: Changzhou was taken. He advanced to suppress western Zhejiang, captured Changxing, and recovered Huzhou; in each his merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou fell. He pushed into western Zhejiang, took Changxing, and recovered Huzhou—each time with the highest credit.

sentences.zh: 賊走廣德、徽州，合江寧、杭州賊自江西竄閩。

translations.literal: The rebels fled toward Guangde and Huizhou; those from Jiangning and Hangzhou, joining with rebels from Jiangxi, slipped into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled toward Guangde and Huizhou; forces from Nanjing and Hangzhou, mingling with rebels from Jiangxi, broke into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 四年，李鴻章檄松林率五千人航海赴援，克漳州、漳浦、雲霄、詔安，賊竄廣東嘉應，遂破滅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Li Hongzhang ordered Songlin to lead five thousand men by sea to the relief. He took Zhangzhou, Zhangpu, Yunxiao, and Zhao'an; the rebels fled to Jiaying in Guangdong and were finally destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 Li Hongzhang ordered Songlin to sail south with five thousand men. He took Zhangzhou, Zhangpu, Yunxiao, and Zhao'an; the rebels fled to Jiaying in Guangdong and were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 五年，曾國荃調松林率新募湘軍剿捻匪於德安，克應城、雲夢，复敗之皁河、楊澤。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Zeng Guoquan transferred Songlin to lead newly recruited Xiang troops in suppressing Nian bandits at De'an. He took Yingcheng and Yunmeng and again defeated them at Zaohe and Yangze.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 Zeng Guoquan sent Songlin with fresh Hunan recruits to fight the Nian at De'an. He took Yingcheng and Yunmeng and beat them again at Zaohe and Yangze.

sentences.zh: 追至臼口，中伏，松林傷足，臥地不能起。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Jiukou, they fell into an ambush. Songlin was wounded in the foot and lay on the ground unable to rise.
translations.idiomatic: In the pursuit to Jiukou they walked into an ambush. Songlin was shot in the foot and could not get up.

sentences.zh: 將卒不見松林，复闖入陣，負而出之。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers, not seeing Songlin, charged back into the battle line and carried him out on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: When his men could not find him, they plunged back into the fight and carried him out.

sentences.zh: 弟芳珍戰死。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fangzhen died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fangzhen was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 松林以創重假歸。

translations.literal: Songlin took leave to return home because of the severity of his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Songlin went home on leave to recover from his wounds.

sentences.zh: 六年，創愈，李鴻章令統萬人號武毅軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when his wounds had healed, Li Hongzhang ordered him to command ten thousand men under the name Wuyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867, once he had healed, Li Hongzhang put him in command of ten thousand men as the Wuyi Army.

sentences.zh: 時東捻任柱已斃，餘黨走壽光，松林要擊，破之杞城。

translations.literal: By then the eastern Nian leader Ren Zhu was already dead; the remnant band fled to Shouguang. Songlin intercepted them and defeated them at Qicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern Nian chief Ren Zhu was already dead; the survivors fled to Shouguang. Songlin cut them off and crushed them at Qicheng.

sentences.zh: 賊沿海南走，阻瀰河，捻酋牛喜子麾白旗賊犯劉銘傳軍；

translations.literal: The rebels fled south along the coast and were blocked at the Mi River. The Nian chief Niu Xizi led White Banner rebels against Liu Mingchuan's army;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled down the coast and were stopped at the Mi River. The Nian chief Niu Xizi led the White Banner force against Liu Mingchuan;

sentences.zh: 賴文光麾藍旗賊犯松林軍。

translations.literal: Lai Wenguang led Blue Banner rebels against Songlin's army.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Wenguang led the Blue Banner force against Songlin.

sentences.zh: 兩軍縱擊，賊大潰，壽光民圩皆出助殺，賊赴瀰河死，浮屍二萬餘，俘萬餘人，奪獲騾馬二萬匹。

translations.literal: Both armies charged freely; the rebels broke in great disorder. The fortified villages around Shouguang all came out to help kill them. Rebels who rushed into the Mi River died; more than twenty thousand corpses floated on the water; more than ten thousand were captured; twenty thousand mules and horses were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides let loose the pursuit and the rebels collapsed. Villagers around Shouguang turned out to help slaughter them. Thousands drowned in the Mi River; more than twenty thousand bodies floated on the water, more than ten thousand were taken alive, and twenty thousand pack animals were captured.

sentences.zh: 賊酋徐昌先、范汝增、任定皆伏誅。

translations.literal: The rebel chiefs Xu Changxian, Fan Ruzeng, and Ren Ding were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chiefs Xu Changxian, Fan Ruzeng, and Ren Ding were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 賴文光鳧水南奔，松林疾馳六百里，追至清江。

translations.literal: Lai Wenguang fled south across the water. Songlin galloped six hundred li in haste and pursued him to Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Wenguang fled south across the rivers. Songlin raced six hundred li in pursuit as far as Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 文光死奔，至揚州瓦窯鋪，為吳毓蘭所擒。

translations.literal: Wenguang fled for his life to Wayao pu in Yangzhou, where Wu Yulan captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenguang fled headlong to Wayao post station near Yangzhou, where Wu Yulan seized him.

sentences.zh: 東捻平。

translations.literal: The eastern Nian were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern Nian rebellion was ended.

sentences.zh: 七年春，西捻犯畿輔，松林敗之安平，再破之茌平。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year the western Nian invaded the capital region. Songlin defeated them at Anping and again at Chiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1868 the western Nian raided the capital districts. Songlin beat them at Anping and again at Chiping.

sentences.zh: 自臨邑築長圍至馬頰河，松林偕潘鼎新、王心安守之，敗賊於海豐，追至德州，歷十六晝夜，斬捕過半。

translations.literal: From Linyi they built a long encirclement to the Majia River. Songlin, together with Pan Dingxin and Wang Xin'an, held it, defeated the rebels at Haifeng, pursued them to Dezhou, and over sixteen days and nights killed and captured more than half.
translations.idiomatic: From Linyi they threw a long cordon to the Majia River, which Songlin held with Pan Dingxin and Wang Xin'an. They routed the rebels at Haifeng, chased them to Dezhou, and in sixteen days and nights killed or captured more than half the force.

sentences.zh: 六月，松林會潘鼎新大破之沙河，俘斬四千。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Songlin joined Pan Dingxin in a great defeat of the rebels at Shahe; four thousand were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he and Pan Dingxin shattered the rebels at Shahe, killing or capturing four thousand.

sentences.zh: 捻走黃、運、徒駭河間，松林與銘傳縱橫要擊，張總愚赴水死。

translations.literal: The Nian fled among the Huang, Yun, and Tuhai rivers. Songlin and Mingchuan struck them at every turn; Zhang Zongyu threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian fled among the Huang, Yun, and Tuhai rivers. Songlin and Mingchuan cut them off wherever they turned; Zhang Zongyu drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，賜黃馬褂，予輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: The western Nian were pacified. He was granted the yellow riding jacket and given the hereditary office of Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: With the western Nian suppressed, he received the yellow riding jacket and a hereditary Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 授湖北提督，調直隸。

translations.literal: He was appointed provincial military commander of Hubei and transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was made provincial military commander of Hubei, then transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，卒於官，優恤，建專祠，諡武壯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he died in office. Exceptional mourning honors were granted, a special shrine was built, and he was given the posthumous title Martial and Strong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 1880. The court granted exceptional mourning honors, built him a special shrine, and gave him the posthumous title Wuzhuang.

sentences.zh: 李長樂，字漢春，安徽盱眙人。

translations.literal: Li Changle, courtesy name Hanchun, was a native of Xuyi in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changle, style name Hanchun, was from Xuyi in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以外委從郭松林隸淮軍，充營官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, as an acting sub-officer he followed Guo Songlin into the Huai Army and served as battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, as an acting sub-officer, he followed Guo Songlin into the Huai Army and served as battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 克柘林、奉賢、南匯、川沙、金山，解松江圍，复青浦，擢千總。

translations.literal: He captured Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, and Jinshan, lifted the siege of Songjiang, recovered Qingpu, and was promoted to sergeant.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, and Jinshan, raised the siege of Songjiang, recovered Qingpu, and was promoted to sergeant.

sentences.zh: 戰四江口，松林軍方泰鎮，長樂率所部深入，近賊壘。

translations.literal: In the battle at Sijiangkou, Songlin's army was at Fangtai zhen. Changle led his unit deep in and came close to the rebel fort.
translations.idiomatic: At Sijiangkou, while Songlin's main force was at Fangtai, Changle led his men deep into rebel territory until they were almost on the enemy stockade.

sentences.zh: 夜半，趣軍士起，曰：「今陷賊中，旦明賊覺，無得脫者。

translations.literal: At midnight he urged the soldiers to rise and said: "We are now trapped among the rebels; when dawn comes and they discover us, none will escape.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he roused his men and said, "We are trapped in the middle of the enemy camp. At dawn they will find us, and none of us will get out.

sentences.zh: 盍出奇計劫之！

translations.literal: Why not use a surprise stratagem to raid them!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not strike first with a surprise raid?"

sentences.zh: 」遂投火賊幕，鼓角乘之，賊驚擾，長樂奮呼進，大破之。

translations.literal: He then set fire to the rebel tents, followed with drums and horns, and the rebels were thrown into alarm and disorder. Changle charged forward with a fierce shout and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: He set fire to the rebel tents, sounded drums and horns, and threw the camp into panic. Changle led the charge with a battle cry and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 又設伏黃渡，擊之半濟，又敗之吳淞江南。

translations.literal: He also laid an ambush at Huangdu, struck them mid-crossing, and again defeated them south of the Wusong River.
translations.idiomatic: He ambushed them at Huangdu as they were crossing the river, then beat them again south of the Wusong.

sentences.zh: 四江口圍解，擢都司，賜花翎。

translations.literal: The siege at Sijiangkou was lifted. He was promoted to company commander and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The siege at Sijiangkou was raised. He was promoted to company commander and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二年，進屯常熟王莊，援賊踞陳市，阻官軍進路。

translations.literal: In the second year he advanced and encamped at Wangzhuang in Changshu. Relief rebels held Chen shi and blocked the government army's advance.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he advanced to Wangzhuang near Changshu. Rebel reinforcements held Chen market and blocked the government advance.

sentences.zh: 從松林自南漍攻賊右，連破賊營，直趨長涇。

translations.literal: Following Songlin he attacked the rebel right from Nangang, broke their camps in succession, and drove straight toward Changjing.
translations.idiomatic: With Songlin he attacked the rebel right from Nangang, stormed camp after camp, and pushed straight for Changjing.

sentences.zh: 長樂陷陣傷脛，裹創力戰敗賊，擢參將，賜號侃勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Changle was first into the enemy line and wounded in the shin; he bound the wound and fought on fiercely to defeat the rebels. He was promoted to brigade commander and granted the title Valiant Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: Changle led the charge and took a shin wound; he bound it and fought on until the rebels broke. He was promoted to brigade commander and given the title Valiant Baturu.

sentences.zh: 尋克江陰，規無錫，出新塘橋。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jiangyin was taken. He planned for Wuxi and advanced from Xintang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin fell soon after. He turned toward Wuxi and advanced from Xintang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 賊憑壘鳴砲俯擊，長樂濡絮裹身越溝進，敗之；

translations.literal: The rebels relied on their fort and fired cannon down on them. Changle soaked cotton padding, wrapped his body, crossed the ditch to advance, and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the fort and raked them with cannon fire. Changle padded himself with wet cotton, crossed the ditch under fire, and routed them;

sentences.zh: 逐奔至亭子橋，刺賊酋黃子隆中肩，又設伏兵敗援賊。

translations.literal: pursued the fleeing enemy to Tingzi Bridge, stabbed the rebel chief Huang Zilong in the shoulder, and again set an ambush to defeat relief rebels.
translations.idiomatic: pursued them to Tingzi Bridge, stabbed the rebel chief Huang Zilong in the shoulder, and ambushed and broke the relief column.

sentences.zh: 李秀成圍大橋角營，從松林往援，奪其舟，賊退走，盡平梅村諸壘。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng besieged the camp at Daqiaojiao. Changle followed Songlin to the relief, seized their boats, and the rebels retreated; all the forts around Meicun were leveled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng besieged the camp at Daqiaojiao. Changle went with Songlin to relieve it, seized the rebel boats, and drove them off until every fort around Meicun was cleared.

sentences.zh: 會諸軍圍攻無錫，率輕騎掩至，梯城入，黃子隆就擒，長樂獲其子德懋。

translations.literal: When the allied armies besieged Wuxi, he led light cavalry in a surprise approach, scaled the wall with ladders and entered. Huang Zilong was captured, and Changle took his son Demao.
translations.idiomatic: In the joint siege of Wuxi he led light cavalry in a surprise dash, scaled the walls on ladders, and took Huang Zilong prisoner along with his son Demao.

sentences.zh: 尋坐失察部勇，褫職留軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was punished for failure to supervise his troops properly; his office was stripped but he remained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon stripped of rank for lax discipline among his men but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 進規常州，援總兵唐殿魁於奔牛，解其圍。

translations.literal: He advanced to plan for Changzhou, relieved Major General Tang Diankui at Benniu, and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the campaign against Changzhou, relieved Major General Tang Diankui at Benniu, and broke the siege there.

sentences.zh: 三年，敗賊上湖橋，克宜興，复官。

translations.literal: In the third year he defeated rebels at Shanghu Bridge, captured Yixing, and was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he routed the rebels at Shanghu Bridge, took Yixing, and was restored to rank.

sentences.zh: 移軍溧陽、金壇，戰皆捷。

translations.literal: He shifted his army to Liyang and Jintan; every battle was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his force to Liyang and Jintan and won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 回援常熟，解其圍，連破賊於楊舍、華墅、周莊、三河口，會攻常州。

translations.literal: He returned to relieve Changshu and lifted the siege, defeated rebels in succession at Yangshe, Huashu, Zhouzhuang, and Sanhekou, and joined in the attack on Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back to raise the siege of Changshu, beat the rebels in turn at Yangshe, Huashu, Zhouzhuang, and Sanhekou, and joined the assault on Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，合圍，長樂先登，賊酋陳坤書、黃和錦就擒，復常州，擢副將，賜號尚勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the encirclement closed. Changle was first over the wall; the rebel chiefs Chen Kunshu and Huang Hejin were captured. Changzhou was recovered; he was promoted to deputy commander and granted the title Esteemed Brave Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the ring closed. Changle was first over the wall; the rebel chiefs Chen Kunshu and Huang Hejin were taken. Changzhou was recovered, he was made deputy commander, and he received the title Esteemed Brave Baturu.

sentences.zh: 從松林進克浙江長興，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: Following Songlin he advanced to capture Changxing in Zhejiang and was recorded for appointment as major general.
translations.idiomatic: With Songlin he advanced into Zhejiang and took Changxing, and was entered on the rolls for major general.

sentences.zh: 進湖州，破呂山賊。

translations.literal: He advanced on Huzhou and defeated rebels at Lüshan.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on Huzhou and routed the rebels at Lüshan.

sentences.zh: 攻賊酋黃文金於尹隆橋，官軍不利，長樂率三營別屯李家港，保糧道。

translations.literal: Attacking the rebel chief Huang Wenjin at Yinlong Bridge, the government army fared poorly. Changle led three battalions to encamp separately at Lijia gang and protect the grain route.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on the rebel chief Huang Wenjin at Yinlong Bridge the government forces faltered. Changle took three battalions to a separate camp at Lijia harbor to hold the supply line.

sentences.zh: 賊傾巢來爭，長樂偕易用剛夾擊之，斬賊酋黃十四，破尹隆橋，遂復湖州。

translations.literal: The rebels came out in full force to contest it. Changle, together with Yi Yonggang, struck them from both sides, beheaded the rebel chief Huang Fourteen, broke Yinlong Bridge, and thus recovered Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threw their full strength at him. Changle and Yi Yonggang caught them in a pincer, killed the rebel chief Huang Fourteen, broke Yinlong Bridge, and recovered Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年春，從松林援福建，戰於海澄赤嶺。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he followed Songlin to relieve Fujian and fought at Chiling in Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1865 he followed Songlin to Fujian and fought at Chiling in Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 松林分兵為八隊，長樂居中當賊首李世賢，破走之，竄漳州。

translations.literal: Songlin divided his force into eight columns. Changle held the center against the rebel chief Li Shixian, routed him, and drove him fleeing toward Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Songlin split his force into eight columns. Changle took the center against the rebel chief Li Shixian, broke him, and drove him toward Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 長樂進屯古田，據山東形勝，賊悉銳力爭，擊卻之，复漳浦、雲霄。

translations.literal: Changle advanced and encamped at Gutian, holding the strategic heights east of the mountains. The rebels brought all their elite strength to contest it; he beat them back and recovered Zhangpu and Yunxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Changle advanced to Gutian and seized the heights to the east. The rebels threw their best troops at him; he drove them off and recovered Zhangpu and Yunxiao.

sentences.zh: 南趨詔安，破之梅村，復其城，加提督銜。

translations.literal: He pressed south toward Zhao'an, defeated the rebels at Meicun, recovered the city, and was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed south to Zhao'an, routed the rebels at Meicun, recovered the city, and received brevet provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 福建平，旋師江蘇，屯鎮江。

translations.literal: Fujian was pacified. The army turned back to Jiangsu and encamped at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: With Fujian pacified, the army returned to Jiangsu and encamped at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓督師剿捻匪，松林已歸，長樂代將其眾以從，兼統忠樸三營，為游擊之師，轉戰河南、山東間。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan commanded the suppression of Nian bandits, Songlin had already returned home. Changle took command of his troops in his place and also commanded the three battalions of Zhongpu, serving as a mobile strike force and campaigning between Henan and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan took command against the Nian, Songlin had gone home. Changle led his old troops in his stead, also took the three Zhongpu battalions as a mobile strike force, and fought back and forth between Henan and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 六年，李鴻章代國籓督師，松林復至軍，增松林軍至二十餘營，號武毅軍，長樂所部曰武毅軍前軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Li Hongzhang replaced Guofan in command. Songlin returned to the army; Songlin's force was increased to more than twenty battalions under the name Wuyi Army, and Changle's unit was called the Wuyi Army vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 Li Hongzhang replaced Guofan as commander. Songlin rejoined the army, which was expanded to more than twenty battalions as the Wuyi Army; Changle's command became its vanguard.

sentences.zh: 破任柱於贛榆，要賴文光於濰縣，長樂等並力奮擊，賊鳧水東走，躡至餘家寨，賊受創甚鉅，复要之壽光南北洋河、巨瀰河間，擒斬三萬，文光竄揚州被擒，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Ren Zhu was defeated at Ganyu. Lai Wenguang was intercepted at Weixian. Changle and the others joined in a fierce assault; the rebels fled east across the water. The pursuit reached Yujia zhai; the rebels suffered very heavy losses. They were intercepted again between the north and south Yang Rivers and the great Mi River at Shouguang; thirty thousand were captured or killed. Wenguang fled to Yangzhou and was captured. Changle was granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: They broke Ren Zhu at Ganyu and caught Lai Wenguang at Weixian. Changle and the others hammered the rebels until they fled east across the rivers; the pursuit reached Yujia stockade and inflicted crippling losses. At Shouguang, between the Yang and Mi rivers, thirty thousand were killed or captured. Wenguang fled to Yangzhou and was taken. Changle received the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 七年，從剿西捻，戰安平，馬軍失利，長樂等以步卒馳援，賊大潰；

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed in suppressing the western Nian. At Anping the cavalry fared poorly; Changle and the others rushed infantry to the relief and the rebels broke in great disorder;
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he joined the campaign against the western Nian. At Anping the cavalry faltered; Changle rushed his infantry to the rescue and the rebels collapsed;

sentences.zh: 追至饒陽楊家村，又要之深州李家村，破其馬隊，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: the pursuit reached Yangjia cun in Raoyang, and they intercepted them again at Lijia cun in Shenzhou, broke their cavalry, and killed and captured beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: the pursuit ran to Yangjia village in Raoyang and cut them off again at Lijia village in Shenzhou, shattered their cavalry, and killed or captured beyond count.

sentences.zh: 三月，敗賊大坯山。

translations.literal: In the third month he defeated rebels at Dapishan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he routed the rebels at Dapishan.

sentences.zh: 援提督陳振邦於大河村，解其圍，追挫之茌平、滄州，援副都統春壽於海豐郝家寨。

translations.literal: He relieved Provincial Military Commander Chen Zhenbang at Dahe cun and lifted the siege, pursued and checked them at Chiping and Cangzhou, and relieved Vice Commander Chun Shou at Haojia zhai in Haifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved Provincial Military Commander Chen Zhenbang at Dahe village, raised the siege, harried the rebels at Chiping and Cangzhou, and relieved Vice Commander Chun Shou at Haojia stockade in Haifeng.

sentences.zh: 六月，追至樂陵，擒總愚子正江、弟得華，戰商河，槍傷總愚。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the pursuit reached Leling; Zongyu's son Zhengjiang and younger brother Dehua were captured. At Shanghe Zongyu was wounded by gunfire.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the pursuit reached Leling, where Zongyu's son Zhengjiang and brother Dehua were taken. At Shanghe Zongyu was shot.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，以提督總兵遇缺題奏，晉博奇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When the western Nian were pacified, he was memorialized for appointment as provincial military commander or major general whenever a vacancy occurred, and was advanced to Boqi Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: With the western Nian suppressed, he was recommended for the next provincial commander or major general vacancy and advanced to Boqi Baturu.

sentences.zh: 十年，署湖北提督，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he acted as provincial military commander of Hubei and soon received the substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he served as acting provincial military commander of Hubei and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，調湖南。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he was transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879 he was transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 六年，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In 1880 he was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 近畿海防重要，奏令長樂駐蘆臺，扼大沽、北塘門戶。

translations.literal: Coastal defense near the capital was important; a memorial ordered Changle to garrison Lutai and hold the gateways of Dagu and Beitang.
translations.idiomatic: Because coastal defense near the capital mattered greatly, the court ordered Changle to garrison Lutai and guard the approaches to Dagu and Beitang.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒官，優恤，諡勤勇。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died in office. Exceptional mourning honors were granted, and he was given the posthumous title Diligent and Brave.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 1889. The court granted exceptional mourning honors and the posthumous title Qinyong.

sentences.zh: 楊鼎勳，字少銘，四川華陽人。

translations.literal: Yang Dingxun, courtesy name Shaoming, was a native of Huayang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dingxun, style name Shaoming, was from Huayang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，應募從軍，初隸湖北按察使李孟群，克漢陽，擢把總。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he answered the call to enlist, first serving under Li Mengqun, judicial commissioner of Hubei. Hanyang was taken and he was promoted to corporal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he enlisted, first under Li Mengqun, judicial commissioner of Hubei. When Hanyang fell he was promoted to corporal.

sentences.zh: 七年，隸提督鮑超軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered the army of Provincial Military Commander Bao Chao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he joined the army of Provincial Military Commander Bao Chao.

sentences.zh: 八年，戰湖口，擢千總。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he fought at Hukou and was promoted to sergeant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he fought at Hukou and was promoted to sergeant.

sentences.zh: 十年，鮑超與陳玉成大戰小池驛，鼎勳見玉成立陣中指揮，獨從壯士十數人突前擊之，玉成駭走，复太湖、潛山兩城。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Bao Chao fought a great battle with Chen Yucheng at Xiaochi yi. Dingxun saw Yucheng standing in the battle line directing; he alone led a dozen stalwarts in a sudden forward assault. Yucheng fled in alarm, and Taihu and Qianshan were both recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Bao Chao fought Chen Yucheng at Xiaochi post station. Dingxun saw Yucheng directing from the line, led a dozen picked men in a headlong charge, and sent Yucheng fleeing in panic. Taihu and Qianshan were recovered.

sentences.zh: 敘功，賜花翎。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was commended and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 李秀成踞黟縣，鼎勳擊賊城下，奪門入，大軍繼之，復其城。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng held Yi county. Dingxun attacked the rebels below the wall, seized the gate and entered; the main army followed, and the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng held Yi county. Dingxun assaulted the walls, forced the gate, and broke in; the main force followed and the city was retaken.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復建德，擢都司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Jiande was recovered and he was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he helped recover Jiande and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 破安慶赤岡嶺賊壘，擢游擊。

translations.literal: He stormed the rebel fort at Chigang Ridge near Anqing and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took the rebel stronghold at Chigang Ridge outside Anqing and was made battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 初，小池驛之戰，鮑超嘉其功，令將五百人，所向有功。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the battle of Xiaochi post station, Bao Chao praised his merit and ordered him to command five hundred men; wherever he went there was achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the fight at Xiaochi post station, Bao Chao commended him and put five hundred men under his command; he won success wherever he was sent.

sentences.zh: 諸將嫉之，譖於超。

translations.literal: The other commanders envied him and slandered him to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Other officers grew jealous and brought accusations against him to Bao Chao.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章督師上海，遂去超從淮軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang directed the army at Shanghai; Dingxun then left Chao and followed the Huai Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, when Li Hongzhang took command at Shanghai, Dingxun left Bao Chao and joined the Huai Army.

sentences.zh: 虹橋、四江口諸戰有功，累擢副將。

translations.literal: At Hongqiao, Sikou, and other battles he rendered merit and was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself at Hongqiao, Sikou, and other engagements and rose step by step to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 募淮勇千人，號勳字軍，屯金山張堰，扼平湖乍浦要衝，習西洋槍隊，每戰輒為軍鋒。

translations.literal: He recruited a thousand Huai braves, styled them the Xun Character Army, encamped at Zhangyan in Jinshan, and held the strategic crossing of Pinghu and Zhapu. They drilled in Western musket companies and in every battle served as the army's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a thousand Huai braves as the Xun Character Army, posted them at Zhangyan in Jinshan to block the Pinghu–Zhapu corridor, trained them in Western musket tactics, and in every fight led the van.

sentences.zh: 二年，破新昌賊壘，連克楓涇，斬賊四千，生擒五百；

translations.literal: In the second year he stormed the rebel fort at Xinchang, took Fengjing in succession, beheaded four thousand rebels, and captured five hundred alive;
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he smashed the rebel fort at Xinchang, took Fengjing in turn, killed four thousand rebels, and took five hundred prisoners;

sentences.zh: 再戰西塘，裹創奮擊，大敗之，擢總兵，賜號鋒勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He fought again at Xitang, bound his wounds and struck fiercely, and routed them utterly. He was promoted to major general and granted the title Sharp Brave Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: At Xitang he fought on despite his wounds, routed the enemy, was made major general, and received the title Sharp Brave Baturu.

sentences.zh: 從程學啟規蘇州，鼎勳攻下城外堅壘，蘇州复，加提督銜。

translations.literal: Following Cheng Xueqi in the plan against Suzhou, Dingxun stormed the stout forts outside the walls. Suzhou was recovered and he was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: With Cheng Xueqi in the campaign for Suzhou, Dingxun carried the outer forts; when Suzhou fell he received brevet provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，會克宜興、荊溪、溧陽，解常熟、無錫圍。

translations.literal: In the third year he joined in taking Yixing, Jingxi, and Liyang and lifted the sieges of Changshu and Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he helped take Yixing, Jingxi, and Liyang and raise the sieges of Changshu and Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 攻常州，賊因蘇州之殺降，惟死守。

translations.literal: In the attack on Changzhou, because of the massacre of surrendered men at Suzhou, the rebels could only hold on to the death.
translations.idiomatic: At Changzhou the rebels, remembering how surrendered men had been killed at Suzhou, fought only to hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 鼎勳以蜀人將淮勇，懼諸將輕己，每戰輒先，晝夜環攻，盡毀城外賊壘，血戰三日。

translations.literal: Dingxun, a Sichuan man commanding Huai braves, feared the other commanders would look down on him; in every battle he took the lead. Day and night he pressed the encirclement, destroyed all the rebel forts outside the walls, and fought a bloody battle for three days.
translations.idiomatic: A Sichuanese leading Huai troops, Dingxun feared his peers would slight him and always led the charge. For three days and nights he ringed the city, tore down every outer rebel fort, and fought hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 造浮橋，率死士先登城，砲彈洞胸達背，左右扶之，絕而復蘇，遂克常州，以提督記名簡放。

translations.literal: He built a pontoon bridge and led dare-to-die men in the first ascent of the wall. A cannonball pierced his chest through to his back; those at his sides supported him. He lost consciousness and revived, and Changzhou was taken. He was recorded for appointment as provincial military commander and selected for release.
translations.idiomatic: He threw a pontoon bridge across the moat and led stormers up first. A round went through his chest and out his back; his men caught him as he collapsed, then he came to and the city fell. He was entered on the rolls for provincial military commander and marked for appointment.

sentences.zh: 創愈，進克浦口，复長興，招降湖州賊黨，會克其城。

translations.literal: When his wounds healed he advanced and took Pukou, recovered Changxing, induced the rebel faction at Huzhou to surrender, and joined in taking that city.
translations.idiomatic: Once healed he took Pukou, recovered Changxing, won over the rebel bands at Huzhou, and helped capture the city.

sentences.zh: 追賊至皖境，克廣德。

translations.literal: He pursued the rebels into Anhui territory and took Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: He chased the rebels into Anhui and captured Guangde.

sentences.zh: 四年，偕郭松林援福建，攻烏頭門賊壘，复漳州，授江蘇蘇松鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went with Guo Songlin to reinforce Fujian, stormed the rebel fort at Wutou Gate, recovered Zhangzhou, and was appointed major general of the Susong Garrison in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he joined Guo Songlin in Fujian, took the rebel stronghold at Wutou Gate, recovered Zhangzhou, and was made major general of the Jiangsu Susong garrison.

sentences.zh: 五年，調赴河南剿捻匪，敗賊硃仙鎮，躡擊至定陶、睢寧。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Henan to suppress the Nian bandits, defeated the rebels at Zhuxian town, and pursued them to Dingtao and Suining.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he was sent to Henan against the Nian, routed them at Zhuxian, and chased them to Dingtao and Suining.

sentences.zh: 六年，破賊於黃陂、孝感，擢浙江提督，調湖南。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he defeated the rebels at Huangpi and Xiaogan, was promoted to provincial military commander of Zhejiang, and was transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he beat the rebels at Huangpi and Xiaogan, was made provincial military commander of Zhejiang, and then transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十月，破賊於山東濰縣，追至​​夏灣，賊酋陳懷忠乞降，分軍出周家寨襲賊，大破之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he defeated the rebels at Weixian in Shandong, pursued them to Xiawan, and the rebel chief Chen Huaizhong begged to surrender. He divided his force to sally from Zhoujiazhai and strike the rebels, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he routed the rebels at Weixian in Shandong and pursued them to Xiawan, where the rebel chief Chen Huaizhong offered to surrender. He detached a column from Zhoujiazhai to fall on the enemy and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 追擊於諸城、膠州。

translations.literal: He pursued them at Zhucheng and Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the pursuit through Zhucheng and Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 東捻平，論功，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were pacified, his merit was assessed and he was granted a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry rank.
translations.idiomatic: With the eastern Nian suppressed, he was rewarded with a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry office.

sentences.zh: 七年，馳援畿輔，破捻匪於安平，追至楊家村，降賊酋張志清。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he rushed to reinforce the capital region, defeated the Nian bandits at Anping, pursued them to Yangjia village, and the rebel chief Zhang Zhiqing surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he hurried north to the capital districts, routed the Nian at Anping, chased them to Yangjia village, and accepted the surrender of the rebel chief Zhang Zhiqing.

sentences.zh: 偕郭松林擊賊濬縣大邳山，又敗之衛輝，陣斬賊酋王建瀛、熊八，擒悍賊何士喜、周久於龍王廟。

translations.literal: With Guo Songlin he struck the rebels at Dapi Mountain in Jun county, defeated them again at Weihui, slew the rebel chiefs Wang Jianying and Xiong Ba in battle, and captured the fierce rebels He Shixi and Zhou Jiu at Longwang Temple.
translations.idiomatic: With Guo Songlin he fought the rebels at Dapi Mountain in Jun county, beat them again at Weihui, killed the rebel chiefs Wang Jianying and Xiong Ba on the field, and seized the hardened fighters He Shixi and Zhou Jiu at Longwang Temple.

sentences.zh: 賊竄山東，自德州趨天津，鼎勳守運河，修牆浚壕，賊來犯，輒擊走之。

translations.literal: The rebels fled into Shandong and from Dezhou pressed toward Tianjin. Dingxun guarded the Grand Canal, repaired the walls and deepened the moats, and whenever the rebels came to attack he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slipped into Shandong and marched from Dezhou toward Tianjin. Dingxun held the Grand Canal line, strengthened the walls and ditches, and beat back every assault.

sentences.zh: 會舊傷發，遽卒，數日而西捻平。

translations.literal: His old wounds flared up and he died suddenly; within days the western Nian were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: His old wounds reopened and he died suddenly; a few days later the western Nian were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏聞，贈太子少保，諡忠勤，建專祠。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized the throne. He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous title Loyal and Diligent, and a dedicated shrine was built.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang reported his death to the court. He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous title Loyal and Diligent, and granted a private shrine.

sentences.zh: 唐殿魁，字藎臣，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Tang Diankui, courtesy name Jinchen, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Diankui, style name Jinchen, was from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，巡撫翁同書檄率鄉團援壽州，力解城圍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng Governor Weng Tongshu ordered him by dispatch to lead local militia to relieve Shouzhou, and he strenuously lifted the siege of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Governor Weng Tongshu summoned him to lead local militia to Shouzhou, where he broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 又從克合肥三河汛，解六安圍，敘千總。

translations.literal: He also followed in the capture of the Sanhe garrison at Hefei, lifted the siege of Lu'an, and was commended with the rank of sergeant.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped take the Sanhe garrison outside Hefei and raise the siege of Lu'an, and was commended as sergeant.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章率淮軍援上海，殿魁從，隸劉銘傳，克南匯、川沙、奉賢、金山衛、柘林五城，積功累擢都司，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang led the Huai Army to reinforce Shanghai; Diankui followed and served under Liu Mingchuan. Nanhui, Chuansha, Fengxian, Jinshanwei, and Zhelin—five cities—were taken. For accumulated merit he was repeatedly promoted to company commander and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, when Li Hongzhang brought the Huai Army to Shanghai, Diankui went with him under Liu Mingchuan and helped take Nanhui, Chuansha, Fengxian, Jinshanwei, and Zhelin. For steady service he rose to company commander and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二年，克江陰楊舍汛城，擢游擊，賜號振勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the second year he took the Yangshe garrison city of Jiangyin, was promoted to battalion commander, and granted the title Striking Brave Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he captured the Yangshe garrison at Jiangyin, was made battalion commander, and received the title Striking Brave Baturu.

sentences.zh: 复江陰縣城，擢參將。

translations.literal: Jiangyin county seat was recovered and he was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangyin city fell he was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 尋克無錫，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Wuxi was taken and he was recorded for appointment as major general.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxi fell soon after, and he was entered on the rolls for major general.

sentences.zh: 從劉銘傳攻常州，銘傳受重傷，令殿魁偕副將黃桂蘭督兵進。

translations.literal: Following Liu Mingchuan in the attack on Changzhou, Mingchuan was badly wounded and ordered Diankui together with Deputy Commander Huang Guilan to direct the troops forward.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Changzhou, Mingchuan was badly wounded and sent Diankui with Deputy Commander Huang Guilan to lead the advance.

sentences.zh: 甫至奔牛鎮，而常州、丹陽兩路賊麕至，圍之。

translations.literal: He had just reached Benniu town when rebel forces from both the Changzhou and Danyang routes swarmed in and surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely reached Benniu when rebels from Changzhou and Danyang converged and surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 殿魁據石營依河岸，壁壘悉為賊轟毀，堅守二十餘日。

translations.literal: Diankui held a stone camp along the riverbank; the walls and ramparts were all smashed by rebel bombardment, yet he held firm for more than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Diankui held a stone camp on the riverbank. Rebel fire wrecked his works, but he held out for more than twenty days.

sentences.zh: 銘傳裹創往救，殿魁從內夾擊，苦戰數日，圍始解。

translations.literal: Mingchuan bound his wounds and went to the rescue; Diankui struck from within in a pincer attack. After bitter fighting for several days the encirclement was finally broken.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan came with his wounds still bound; Diankui hit the ring from inside while Mingchuan pressed from without. After days of hard fighting the siege was broken.

sentences.zh: 三年，克常州，生擒賊首陳坤書，以提督記名。

translations.literal: In the third year Changzhou was taken and the rebel chief Chen Kunshu was captured alive. He was recorded for appointment as provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 Changzhou fell and the rebel chief Chen Kunshu was taken alive. Diankui was entered on the rolls for provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，增募所部至三千人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he increased recruitment of his command to three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he expanded his command to three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 從劉銘傳渡淮剿捻匪，破張寨賊壘。

translations.literal: Following Liu Mingchuan he crossed the Huai to suppress the Nian bandits and stormed the rebel fort at Zhangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Mingchuan he crossed the Huai against the Nian and took the rebel fort at Zhangzhai.

sentences.zh: 五年，授浙江衢州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed major general of the Quzhou Garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he was made major general of the Zhejiang Quzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 追賊至湖北，克黃陂。

translations.literal: He pursued the rebels into Hubei and took Huangpi.
translations.idiomatic: He chased the rebels into Hubei and captured Huangpi.

sentences.zh: 捻匪自山東回竄，銘傳督兵追至烏官屯，殿魁繼進，殺賊五百餘。

translations.literal: The Nian bandits doubled back from Shandong. Mingchuan directed the troops in pursuit to Wuguan tun; Diankui pressed on afterward and killed more than five hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian swung back from Shandong, Mingchuan drove them to Wuguan tun and Diankui followed up, killing more than five hundred.

sentences.zh: 六年，調廣西右江鎮。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Youjiang Garrison in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he was transferred to the Guangxi Youjiang garrison.

sentences.zh: 捻首張總愚竄安陸。

translations.literal: The Nian leader Zhang Zongyu fled into Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian chief Zhang Zongyu broke into Anlu.

sentences.zh: 銘傳與鮑超約會戰於永漋河，銘傳欲先出，殿魁請少待，不從。

translations.literal: Mingchuan and Bao Chao agreed to join battle at the Yongzhang River. Mingchuan wished to go out first; Diankui asked him to wait a little, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan and Bao Chao agreed to meet the enemy at the Yongzhang River. Mingchuan wanted to move first; Diankui urged him to hold back, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 超未至，銘軍先遇賊，部將田履安、李錫增戰沒。

translations.literal: Before Chao arrived, the Ming army met the rebels first; the subordinate commanders Tian Lü'an and Li Xizeng fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chao had not yet arrived when the Ming army met the rebels. Subordinates Tian Lü'an and Li Xizeng were killed in action.

sentences.zh: 殿魁戰小挫，受重傷。

translations.literal: Diankui suffered a small setback in battle and was badly wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Diankui's line buckled and he was badly wounded.

sentences.zh: 及聞霆軍大捷，复裹創力戰，遂殞於陣。

translations.literal: When word came of the Ting Army's great victory, he again bound his wounds and fought with all his might, and fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: When news came of a great victory by the Ting Army, he bound his wounds again and fought on until he fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡忠壯，建專祠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry together with a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Commandant rank, given the posthumous title Loyal and Valiant, and a dedicated shrine was built.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted hereditary Commandant of Cavalry and Cloud Cavalry Commandant ranks, given the posthumous title Loyal and Valiant, and honored with a private shrine.

sentences.zh: 唐定奎，字俊侯，殿魁弟。

translations.literal: Tang Dingkui, courtesy name Junhou, was Diankui's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Dingkui, style name Junhou, was Diankui's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 偕兄轉戰江蘇。

translations.literal: Together with his elder brother he campaigned back and forth in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He fought alongside his brother across Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 從劉銘傳剿捻於山東、河南、安徽、湖北，積功累擢副將，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Following Liu Mingchuan he suppressed the Nian in Shandong, Henan, Anhui, and Hubei. For accumulated merit he was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Mingchuan he campaigned against the Nian in Shandong, Henan, Anhui, and Hubei, rose to deputy commander on accumulated merit, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，殿魁戰歿永漋河，定奎方省母回裡，奔赴軍，誓殺賊復仇，遂代領兄舊部，轉戰河南、山東。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi Diankui fell in battle at the Yongzhang River. Dingkui was just visiting his mother at home; he rushed to the army, swore to kill rebels and avenge his brother, and then took command of his brother's old troops, campaigning in Henan and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 Diankui was killed at the Yongzhang River. Dingkui had been home visiting his mother; he hurried back to camp, swore to kill rebels and avenge his brother, took over the old command, and fought on in Henan and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 六年，殄任柱於贛榆，破賴文光於壽光，所部殺賊最多。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he destroyed Ren Zhu at Ganyu, defeated Lai Wenguang at Shouguang, and his command killed more rebels than any other.
translations.idiomatic: That year he destroyed Ren Zhu at Ganyu and routed Lai Wenguang at Shouguang; his troops accounted for more rebel dead than any other unit.

sentences.zh: 東捻平，以提督記名。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were pacified he was recorded for appointment as provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: With the eastern Nian suppressed, he was entered on the rolls for provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 七年，從剿西捻於直隸、山東，賜號呼敦巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed in suppressing the western Nian in Zhili and Shandong and was granted the title Hodun Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he joined the campaign against the western Nian in Zhili and Shandong and received the title Hodun Baturu.

sentences.zh: 銘軍凱旋，告歸終養。

translations.literal: When the Ming army returned in triumph he asked leave to go home and care for his parents until their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming army came home victorious, he asked to retire and support his parents in their old age.

sentences.zh: 九年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 he went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 劉銘傳赴陝西剿回匪，調定奎接統銘武軍，定奎請終制，命俟陝西軍事平，回籍終制。

translations.literal: Liu Mingchuan went to Shaanxi to suppress Muslim rebels; Dingkui was transferred to take over the Mingwu Army. Dingkui asked to complete his mourning period, and was ordered to wait until Shaanxi military affairs were settled, then return home to finish mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Mingchuan went to Shaanxi against Muslim rebels, Dingkui was called to take the Mingwu Army. He asked to complete mourning; the court told him to wait until the Shaanxi campaign ended, then return home to finish the rites.

sentences.zh: 十年，定奎回防徐州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Dingkui returned to garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 Dingkui returned to garrison Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年，日本擾台灣，生番滋事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Japan harassed Taiwan and the raw aborigines stirred up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In 1874 Japan raided Taiwan and indigenous tribes rose in unrest.

sentences.zh: 船政大臣沈葆楨奏請援師，李鴻章薦定奎率所部往。

translations.literal: Naval Affairs Commissioner Shen Baozhen memorialized requesting reinforcements; Li Hongzhang recommended Dingkui to lead his command there.
translations.idiomatic: Naval Affairs Commissioner Shen Baozhen asked for reinforcements, and Li Hongzhang recommended that Dingkui lead his troops to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 七月，至台灣，駐鳳山，擇險分屯。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he reached Taiwan, encamped at Fengshan, and chose defensible points to divide his garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he landed in Taiwan, posted his headquarters at Fengshan, and split his force among defensible positions.

sentences.zh: 龜紋番社引日兵與刺桐腳莊民尋仇相閧，定奎示以兵威，日人引去。

translations.literal: The Guiwen aborigine community led Japanese troops and the villagers of Citongjiao in a feud that flared into a brawl. Dingkui displayed military might and the Japanese withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Guiwen tribe drew in Japanese soldiers to settle a feud with the village of Citongjiao. Dingkui showed force and the Japanese pulled back.

sentences.zh: 時疫流行，士卒先後死千餘人，定奎拊循周至，兵氣不衰，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: An epidemic was raging; more than a thousand soldiers died in succession. Dingkui comforted and encouraged them with thorough care, and army morale did not decline. He was granted the yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: An epidemic swept the camp and killed more than a thousand men, but Dingkui nursed and encouraged his troops so morale held firm, and he was awarded the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 楓港、獅頭諸社番屢出戕害良民，光緒元年，游擊王開俊進剿，中伏死。

translations.literal: The aborigines of Fenggang, Shitou, and other communities repeatedly came out to slaughter innocent civilians. In the first year of Guangxu Battalion Commander Wang Kaijun advanced to suppress them, fell into an ambush, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Aborigines of Fenggang, Shitou, and neighboring communities kept raiding and killing settlers. In 1875 Battalion Commander Wang Kaijun marched against them, was ambushed, and killed.

sentences.zh: 內外番社結黨劫殺，各社就撫，皆懷觀望。

translations.literal: Interior and exterior aborigine communities formed factions to plunder and kill. Each community that came forward for pacification still harbored hesitation and watched from the sidelines.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes inland and along the coast banded together to raid and kill. Those that came in for pacification still held back and watched how things would go.

sentences.zh: 定奎分遣七營屯東港南勢湖，自率四營當其衝，葆楨檄諸軍並聽節制。

translations.literal: Dingkui detached seven battalions to garrison Donggang and Nanshihu; he personally led four battalions to meet the main thrust. Baozhen issued a dispatch that all armies were to obey his command.
translations.idiomatic: Dingkui posted seven battalions at Donggang and Nanshihu and led four battalions against the main threat himself. Baozhen ordered all forces on the island to take his orders.

sentences.zh: 定奎上書陳兵事，略曰：「逆番晝伏莽中，夜燎山頂，精於標槍，伺間輒發。

translations.literal: Dingkui submitted a memorial on military affairs, stating in summary: "The rebellious aborigines hide by day in the thickets and at night light fires on the hilltops. They are skilled with throwing spears and strike whenever they see an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Dingkui wrote to the court on the campaign, saying in brief: "The hostile tribes lie in the bush by day and signal from the hilltops by night. They are expert with javelins and attack at the first chance.

sentences.zh: 專恃深林密箐，狙擊我師，我進彼隱，我退彼見。

translations.literal: They rely entirely on deep forest and dense ravines, sniping at our army: when we advance they hide; when we withdraw they show themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They depend on deep woods and narrow ravines to snipe at our columns—when we advance they vanish, when we pull back they appear.

sentences.zh: 今欲掃其巢穴，必先翦其荊棘。

translations.literal: If we now wish to sweep away their nests, we must first cut down their brambles.
translations.idiomatic: To root out their strongholds we must first clear the undergrowth.

sentences.zh: 宜增募土勇，導引兵丁，隨山刊木，務絕根株，然後分道進兵，草薙擒狝。

translations.literal: We should increase recruitment of native braves to guide the soldiers, cut timber hill by hill, and make sure the roots are utterly removed; only then divide forces and advance, mowing the grass and capturing the beasts.
translations.idiomatic: We should recruit more local scouts to lead regular troops, cut the forest away slope by slope until nothing is left to shelter them, then advance in separate columns and scour the country clean.

sentences.zh: 其有奸民接濟鹽米火藥者，按軍法，庶幾一舉可以成功。

translations.literal: Any treacherous civilians who supply them with salt, rice, or gunpowder should be dealt with under military law; then perhaps in one effort success may be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who supplies them with salt, grain, or powder should be punished under military law; only then may we succeed in a single campaign.

sentences.zh: 」葆楨據以入告。

translations.literal: " Baozhen forwarded it in a memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " Baozhen sent the memorial up to the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是開山進兵，攻克萃山、竹坑、本武諸社。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened the mountains and advanced, storming the communities of Cuishan, Zhukeng, Benwu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then pushed into the hills and took the communities of Cuishan, Zhukeng, Benwu, and others.

sentences.zh: 獅頭社猶負險抗拒，定奎令諸將得險即守，自剿獅頭兩社，別遣師扼斷外援，遂攻下之。

translations.literal: The Shitou community still relied on rugged terrain and resisted. Dingkui ordered the commanders to hold any defensible point they gained. He himself suppressed the two Shitou communities, sent another force separately to cut off outside aid, and then stormed and took them.
translations.idiomatic: The Shitou tribe still held the high ground. Dingkui told his officers to seize and hold every strong point; he attacked the two Shitou villages himself while another column blocked outside help, and the positions fell.

sentences.zh: 移營駐守，被脅十餘社皆歸命，給衣履酒食，譯示朝廷威德，咸受約束。

translations.literal: He shifted camp to garrison the area. More than ten communities that had been coerced all submitted. He gave them clothing, shoes, food, and wine, had the court's majesty and virtue explained through interpreters, and all accepted restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He moved camp to hold the ground. More than ten coerced villages submitted; he gave them clothes, shoes, food, and wine, had the court's authority explained through interpreters, and brought them all under control.

sentences.zh: 設招撫局，示約七條，曰：遵薙發，編戶口，獻凶逆，禁仇殺，立總目，墾番地，設番塾。

translations.literal: He established a pacification bureau and proclaimed seven articles of agreement, namely: observe the shaving of the queue, register households, hand over murderers, forbid feud killings, appoint headmen, open aborigine land to cultivation, and set up aborigine schools.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a pacification office and posted seven rules: adopt the queue, register households, surrender criminals, end blood feuds, appoint headmen, open tribal land to farming, and establish tribal schools.

sentences.zh: 以龜紋番酋充諸社總目，赦其脅從。

translations.literal: He appointed the Guiwen aborigine chief as headman over all the communities and pardoned those who had followed under coercion.
translations.idiomatic: He made the Guiwen chief headman over the tribes and pardoned those who had followed under duress.

sentences.zh: 台南大定，詔褒獎，命內渡休養士卒。

translations.literal: Southern Taiwan was greatly settled. An imperial edict praised and rewarded him, and he was ordered to cross to the mainland and rest his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Taiwan was pacified. The court commended him and ordered him to return to the mainland and rest his troops.

sentences.zh: 授直隸正定鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was appointed major general of the Zhengding Garrison in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was made major general of the Zhili Zhengding garrison.

sentences.zh: 尋擢福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to provincial military commander of the Fujian land forces.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to provincial military commander of Fujian's land forces.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨調兩江總督，奏統所部駐防江陰。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen was transferred to Governor-General of the Two Jiangs and memorialized that Dingkui should command his troops in garrison at Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Baozhen became governor-general of the Two Jiangs, he had Dingkui's troops posted at Jiangyin under his command.

sentences.zh: 九年，傷發乞休，不允。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his wounds flared up and he asked to retire; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 his old wounds reopened and he asked to retire, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 法越用兵事起，海防戒嚴，詔促力疾赴防。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese war broke out, coastal defense was placed on alert, and an edict urged him to go to his post despite illness.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out between France and Vietnam, the coast was put on alert and he was ordered to take up defense despite his illness.

sentences.zh: 十一年，和議定，病請開缺，允之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the peace treaty was settled. He asked on grounds of illness to be relieved of his post, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 peace was made. He asked to be relieved for illness, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，優恤，諡果介。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died. He received preferential condolence payments and was given the posthumous title Resolute and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1887. The court granted special mourning honors and the posthumous title Resolute and Upright.

sentences.zh: 滕嗣武，湖南麻陽人。

translations.literal: Teng Siwu was a native of Mayang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Siwu was from Mayang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從軍湖北。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he joined the army in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianfeng years he enlisted in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十年，小池驛之戰，功多，超擢都司。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, at the battle of Xiaochi post station, his merit was great and he was promoted by special advance to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, at Xiaochi post station, he won high distinction and was promoted straight to company commander.

sentences.zh: 從攻安慶，嗣武率所部扼要築砲壘，壘未成，賊突出萬餘來爭，嗣武力擊破之。

translations.literal: In the attack on Anqing, Siwu led his command to hold a strategic point and build gun emplacements. Before the emplacements were finished, more than ten thousand rebels burst out to contest the position; Siwu struck fiercely and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Anqing he seized a key point and began building batteries. Before the works were finished, more than ten thousand rebels rushed out to take them; Siwu beat them back.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克安慶，敘功擢參將。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Anqing was taken; his merit was recorded and he was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing fell in 1861; he was commended and made brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，改隸淮軍，從李鴻章至上海，解松江圍，賜號偉勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was transferred to the Huai Army, followed Li Hongzhang to Shanghai, lifted the siege of Songjiang, and was granted the title Mighty Brave Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he joined the Huai Army, followed Li Hongzhang to Shanghai, raised the siege of Songjiang, and received the title Mighty Brave Baturu.

sentences.zh: 屯北簳山扼賊衝，賊犯寶山，與諸軍夾擊破之，進拔南匯，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: He encamped at Beigan Mountain to block the rebel thrust. When the rebels attacked Baoshan he joined other armies in a pincer attack and routed them, advanced and took Nanhui, and was recorded for appointment as major general.
translations.idiomatic: He held Beigan Mountain to block the rebel line. When they struck Baoshan he joined a converging attack and drove them off, then took Nanhui and was entered on the rolls for major general.

sentences.zh: 二年，偕程學啟規蘇州，敗賊於正義鎮。

translations.literal: In the second year he joined Cheng Xueqi in the plan against Suzhou and defeated the rebels at Zhengyi town.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he joined Cheng Xueqi in the campaign for Suzhou and routed the rebels at Zhengyi.

sentences.zh: 地當要衝，以嗣武守之，輔以水師，分軍伏橋口伺賊。

translations.literal: The place lay on a vital crossing; Siwu was assigned to hold it, supported by the naval force, with part of the army hidden at the bridge mouth to watch for the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The town stood on a key crossing. Siwu held it with naval support while a detachment lay in ambush at the bridge.

sentences.zh: 崑山賊勢蹙，啟西門遁。

translations.literal: The rebel position at Kunshan grew desperate; they opened the west gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed at Kunshan, the rebels opened the west gate and fled.

sentences.zh: 伏起，水師以巨砲環擊，賊大潰，立復其城。

translations.literal: The ambush rose up; the naval force battered them with great guns on every side; the rebels routed in great disorder and the city was immediately recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush sprang up and the fleet hammered them with heavy guns from all sides. The rebels broke and fled, and the city was retaken at once.

sentences.zh: 移軍會攻江陰。

translations.literal: He shifted his army to join in the attack on Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his troops to join the assault on Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 賊自無錫來援，連營數十，柵壘棋布。

translations.literal: Rebels came from Wuxi to relieve the city; they pitched dozens of linked camps, and stockades and forts were laid out like chess pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements marched from Wuxi, pitching dozens of linked camps with forts and stockades strewn across the field.

sentences.zh: 軍分三路進，嗣武率八營當中路，攻​​麥市橋，以輕兵伏河堤，燃砲毀賊壘，賊潰走，追及之三巴橋，殲獲殆盡。

translations.literal: The army advanced in three columns. Siwu led eight battalions on the center route, attacking Maishi Bridge. Light troops lay in ambush on the river bank; cannon fire was set to destroy rebel forts. The rebels broke and fled; the pursuit reached Sanba Bridge and nearly all were killed or captured.
translations.idiomatic: The force advanced in three columns. Siwu led eight battalions up the center against Maishi Bridge, with light troops hidden on the riverbank. Cannon fire smashed the rebel forts; the enemy broke and fled, and the pursuit to Sanba Bridge killed or captured nearly the entire force.

sentences.zh: 進次無錫城下，賊首李世賢以全軍拒戰。

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped below Wuxi city. The rebel chief Li Shixian met him with his entire army.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to camp below Wuxi, where the rebel chief Li Shixian met him with his full army.

sentences.zh: 嗣武身先士卒，怒馬突陣，敗之謝家橋，又敗之蕩口。

translations.literal: Siwu was first among the soldiers, charging the enemy line on a spirited horse. He defeated them at Xiejia Bridge and again at Dangkou.
translations.idiomatic: Siwu led from the front, charging the enemy line on a spirited horse. He routed them at Xiejia Bridge and again at Dangkou.

sentences.zh: 賊退據硃王橋堅守，嗣武出奇兵襲擊，擒斬千餘，加提督銜。

translations.literal: The rebels fell back and held Zhuhuang Bridge stubbornly. Siwu sent a surprise force to strike them, capturing and killing more than a thousand. He was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to hold Zhuhuang Bridge. Siwu sent a surprise column, killed or captured more than a thousand, and received brevet provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 既而克無錫，以提督記名。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Wuxi was taken and he was recorded for appointment as provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxi fell soon after, and he was entered on the rolls for provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，會攻常州，破援賊於奔牛鎮，攻下宜興、荊溪，嗣武傷右股。

translations.literal: In the third year he joined in the attack on Changzhou, defeated relief rebels at Benniu zhen, and took Yixing and Jingxi. Siwu was wounded in the right thigh.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he joined the assault on Changzhou, beat the relief force at Benniu, and took Yixing and Jingxi. Siwu was wounded in the right thigh.

sentences.zh: 四月，會圍常州，嗣武當南門，砲毀城垣，克之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he joined the siege of Changzhou. Siwu held the south gate; cannon fire destroyed the wall, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he joined the siege of Changzhou. Siwu held the south gate until artillery breached the wall and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 七年，從李鴻章剿捻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Li Hongzhang in suppressing the Nian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he followed Li Hongzhang against the Nian.

sentences.zh: 畿輔事平。

translations.literal: Affairs in the capital region were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting around the capital was over.

sentences.zh: 八年，授湖北鄖陽鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed major general of Yunyang zhen in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he was made major general of Yunyang garrison in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，賜卹，諡武慎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died. Mourning honors were granted, and he was given the posthumous title Martial and Cautious.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1872. The court granted mourning honors and the posthumous title Wushen.

sentences.zh: 駱國忠，安徽鳳陽人。

translations.literal: Luo Guozhong was a native of Fengyang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Guozhong was from Fengyang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初陷於粵匪，授偽職，知賊必敗，陰圖反正。

translations.literal: He had first been trapped among the Cantonese rebels and was given a rebel office. Knowing the rebels were doomed, he secretly plotted to return to the government side.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been swept up among the Taiping rebels and given a rebel post. Convinced they would fail, he secretly planned to defect.

sentences.zh: 常熟久為賊踞，福山與狼山夾江對峙，賊設屯以扼後路，國忠任城守。

translations.literal: Changshu had long been held by rebels. Fushan and Langshan faced each other across the river; the rebels set garrisons to choke the rear route. Guozhong was charged with defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: Changshu had long been in rebel hands. Fushan and Langshan faced each other across the river, and the rebels posted garrisons to block the rear. Guozhong was put in charge of the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章蒞江蘇，兵威日振，國忠因水師游擊周興隆舉城薙發降。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang arrived in Jiangsu and military prestige grew daily. Through Naval Battalion Commander Zhou Xinglong, Guozhong shaved his head and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 Li Hongzhang took command in Jiangsu and government power grew daily. Through Naval Battalion Commander Zhou Xinglong, Guozhong shaved his head in submission and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 鴻章令興隆、國忠選驍健萬人，分守水陸要衝，以防蘇州竄賊。

translations.literal: Hongzhang ordered Xinglong and Guozhong to select ten thousand stalwart men and divide them to hold the vital points by land and water, guarding against rebels slipping out of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang ordered Xinglong and Guozhong to pick ten thousand picked men and post them at the key land and river crossings to block rebel breakouts from Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 福山守賊胡經元、江勝海原約俱降，國忠遣人召之，比至福山，不得入。

translations.literal: The rebel defenders of Fushan, Hu Jingyuan and Jiang Shenghai, had originally agreed to surrender together. Guozhong sent men to summon them, but when they reached Fushan they could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: The Fushan garrison commanders Hu Jingyuan and Jiang Shenghai had agreed to surrender with him, but when Guozhong's messengers reached Fushan they could not get in.

sentences.zh: 國忠夜率兵往，令其弟國孝攻其南，自與興隆攻其北，斷賊登舟之路，槍殪賊將侯得龍，賊舟師遁走。

translations.literal: Guozhong led troops by night. He ordered his younger brother Guoxiao to attack from the south while he himself, with Xinglong, attacked from the north, cutting off the rebels' path to their boats. He shot and killed the rebel general Hou Delong, and the rebel fleet fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong marched by night, sent his brother Guoxiao against the south wall, and with Xinglong struck the north, cutting off escape to the boats. He shot the rebel general Hou Delong, and the rebel fleet fled.

sentences.zh: 經元、勝海殺賊渠數人，率所部出，與國忠合。

translations.literal: Jingyuan and Shenghai killed several rebel chiefs, led their units out, and joined Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan and Shenghai killed several rebel leaders, brought their men out, and joined Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 國孝越重壕毀賊壘；

translations.literal: Guoxiao crossed the deep moat and destroyed rebel forts;
translations.idiomatic: Guoxiao crossed the deep moat and smashed the rebel forts;

sentences.zh: 興隆等分兵盡拔許浦、白茅、徐涇諸壘，賊將錢壽仁亦自太倉率所部二千詣鴻章降。

translations.literal: Xinglong and the others divided their forces and captured all the forts at Xupu, Baimao, and Xujing. The rebel general Qian Shouren also led two thousand of his men from Taicang to surrender to Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xinglong's columns took the forts at Xupu, Baimao, and Xujing one by one, and the rebel general Qian Shouren brought two thousand men from Taicang to surrender to Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 總兵鞠耀乾率師船泊徐涇，千總袁光政入城助守。

translations.literal: Major General Ju Yaoqian led war junks to anchor at Xujing; Sergeant Yuan Guangzheng entered the city to help defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Major General Ju Yaoqian brought his gunboats to Xujing, and Sergeant Yuan Guangzheng entered the city to help hold it.
