sentences.zh: 十二月，李秀成等以眾數万自蘇州來攻，連營十餘裡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Li Xiucheng and others came from Suzhou to attack with a force of tens of thousands, pitching linked camps for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Li Xiucheng marched from Suzhou with tens of thousands of men and pitched a line of camps more than ten li long.

sentences.zh: 國忠乞濟師，常勝軍五百人自海道往援，而賊由江陰再陷福山，聲援隔絕。

translations.literal: Guozhong begged for relief troops. Five hundred men of the Ever-Victorious Army came by sea to aid him, but the rebels from Jiangyin again took Fushan, and support was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong pleaded for reinforcements. Five hundred Ever-Victorious Army men came by sea, but rebels from Jiangyin retook Fushan and cut him off from help.

sentences.zh: 鴻章令潘鼎新、劉銘傳、張樹珊以三千人趨福山，與黃翼升水師並進。

translations.literal: Hongzhang ordered Pan Dingxin, Liu Mingchuan, and Zhang Shushan to hurry three thousand men to Fushan, advancing together with Huang Yisheng's naval force.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang sent Pan Dingxin, Liu Mingchuan, and Zhang Shushan with three thousand men to Fushan, marching in concert with Huang Yisheng's fleet.

sentences.zh: 福山城小而堅，攻之不下。

translations.literal: Fushan was small but stout; they could not take it by assault.
translations.idiomatic: Fushan was small but tough, and the assault would not break it.

sentences.zh: 常熟被圍愈亟，國忠斂兵入城，興隆屯城西虞山相犄角，為死守計。

translations.literal: The siege of Changshu grew more pressing. Guozhong drew his troops into the city; Xinglong encamped on Yushan west of the city so the two positions supported each other, planning to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege of Changshu tightened, Guozhong pulled his men inside the walls while Xinglong camped on Yushan to the west so the two posts could support each other in a fight to the last.

sentences.zh: 二年，賊以砲壞城東垣，國忠力拒不得入，樹雲梯緣城，亦擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the second year the rebels used cannon to breach the eastern wall. Guozhong fought hard to keep them out; they raised scaling ladders against the wall and he beat them back as well.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 rebel artillery smashed the eastern wall, but Guozhong held them out. When they raised scaling ladders he drove them back again.

sentences.zh: 賊增壘掘隧，數道並進，城危甚。

translations.literal: The rebels added forts and dug tunnels, advancing on several routes at once; the city was in grave peril.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threw up more forts and dug tunnels, pressing the attack on several fronts until the city was in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 會鼎新、銘傳諸軍急攻福山，賊分兵赴援，留者僅數千，國忠乃開城出戰，毀賊壘，擒其渠硃衣點。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Dingxin, Mingchuan, and the other armies pressed the attack on Fushan urgently. The rebels divided their force to relieve it; only a few thousand remained. Guozhong then opened the city and gave battle, destroyed rebel forts, and captured their chief Zhuyidian.
translations.idiomatic: While Dingxin and Mingchuan hammered Fushan, the rebels split off a relief column and left only a few thousand men before Changshu. Guozhong sallied out, smashed their forts, and captured the rebel chief Zhuyidian.

sentences.zh: 福山既克，諸軍來會，城圍始解。

translations.literal: Once Fushan was taken, the armies came together and the siege of the city was finally lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Fushan fell the relieving columns joined him and the siege was finally raised.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，優詔嘉獎，擢授國忠副將，加總兵銜，編降眾為忠字八營。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, an exceptional edict praised and rewarded him. Guozhong was promoted to deputy commander and given brevet major general; the surrendered troops were organized as the eight Zhongzi battalions.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory brought an imperial commendation. Guozhong was made deputy commander with brevet major general and his surrendered troops were organized as the eight Zhongzi battalions.

sentences.zh: 會攻江陰，戰甚力，既克，賜號勁勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He joined in the attack on Jiangyin and fought with great force. After it was taken he was granted the title Stalwart Brave Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He fought hard in the assault on Jiangyin, and after the city fell he received the title Stalwart Brave Baturu.

sentences.zh: 署京口水師副將，留守江陰。

translations.literal: He acted as deputy commander of the Jingkou naval force and remained to garrison Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting deputy commander of the Jingkou fleet and stayed to garrison Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 三年，破丹陽援賊，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the third year he defeated relief rebels from Danyang and was recorded for appointment as major general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he broke the Danyang relief force and was entered on the rolls for major general.

sentences.zh: 尋克常州，以積勞傷發，乞假歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Changzhou was taken. Overwork brought on his old wounds and he asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou fell soon after, but overwork reopened his wounds and he went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 五年，從劉銘傳剿捻匪，轉戰湖北、河南、山東，所鄉有功。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Liu Mingchuan in suppressing Nian bandits, campaigning in Hubei, Henan, and Shandong, and wherever he went he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he followed Liu Mingchuan against the Nian, fighting through Hubei, Henan, and Shandong with credit wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 六年，東捻平，以提督記名，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the eastern Nian were pacified. He was recorded for appointment as provincial military commander and granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern Nian were suppressed in 1867 he was entered on the rolls for provincial military commander and awarded the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 九年，銘傳督辦陝西軍務，調國忠從行。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Mingchuan supervised military affairs in Shaanxi and transferred Guozhong to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 Mingchuan took charge of military affairs in Shaanxi and took Guozhong with him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒於乾州軍中，賜卹，諡勇肅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died in the army at Qianzhou. Mourning honors were granted, and he was given the posthumous title Brave and Stern.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp at Qianzhou in 1873. The court granted mourning honors and the posthumous title Yongsu.

sentences.zh: 論曰：郭松林、李長樂、楊鼎勳、滕嗣武皆由湘、楚舊部改隸淮軍，平吳、平捻，卓著聲績。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Guo Songlin, Li Changle, Yang Dingxun, and Teng Siwu all came from old Xiang and Chu units and were transferred to the Huai Army. They pacified Wu and pacified the Nian, achieving outstanding fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: Guo Songlin, Li Changle, Yang Dingxun, and Teng Siwu all came from old Hunan and Hubei units before joining the Huai Army. In pacifying the lower Yangtze and the Nian they won outstanding fame.

sentences.zh: 唐殿魁淮軍驍將，惜未竟功。

translations.literal: Tang Diankui was a fierce general of the Huai Army; it is a pity he did not complete his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Diankui was one of the Huai Army's fiercest fighters, but he died before his work was done.

sentences.zh: 定奎席兄餘光，名位轉出其上，固有幸有不幸哉。

translations.literal: Dingkui rode on his elder brother's remaining glory, and fame and rank in the end surpassed him—is this fortune mixed with misfortune?
translations.idiomatic: Dingkui built on his brother's reputation and ended up with even greater rank and fame—was that good fortune, or ill?

sentences.zh: 駱國忠智勇堅毅，識時為傑，當時名滿江南，成績可紀也。

translations.literal: Luo Guozhong was wise, brave, firm, and resolute; in reading the times he was outstanding. His name filled Jiangnan at the time, and his achievements are worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Guozhong was shrewd, brave, and steadfast, a man who read the moment with rare clarity. His name was known throughout Jiangnan, and his record speaks for itself.
